audit.whatIsWrong: `mid` reads 'if you auto or Q into his E Counter Strike window he dodges it and stuns you' — it treats Counter Strike as dodging Radiant Volley.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS. Radiant Volley and Solar Snare are abilities, not attacks, and land through it at full value. Getting this backwards is expensive in both directions: it tells Mel to stop casting during the one window where casting is completely safe, and it hides the fact that the only thing she actually loses to Counter Strike is her Searing Brilliance empowered autos. The rest of the entry already gets this right (`whys[3]` and `wants.foe[1]` correctly limit it to autos), so `mid` is the outlier.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike eats your autos, not your spells. Keep throwing Radiant Volley and Solar Snare into it; just do not walk into auto range to feed the stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `breakdown.cooldowns` says to 'count it out loud' but never states the Counter Strike cooldown, and no string anywhere gives the Leap Strike number.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — 17 seconds at rank 1 is an enormous punish window and it is the single most useful number in the lane. Leap Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s at 700 range. Both are on disk and neither is used, which is exactly the 'no cooldown-sequencing advice' shape the packet flags elsewhere on this champion.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike 17s at rank 1 down to 9s at rank 5 is the green light; Leap Strike is 8s and only 700 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states the range gap that makes the early game survivable.
audit.why: Leap Strike is 700 range and must target a unit. Radiant Volley is 950 and Solar Snare is 1000. Mel is not merely 'ranged' here — she has 250-300 units of standoff, and Jax needs a minion or ward inside that gap to close it. That converts vague 'keep your distance' advice into a specific number to hold and a specific thing to deny.
audit.corrected: Hold 700+ and deny him a leap target; his Q cannot start the fight from where your Q ends it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The all-in tell is described as 'Q-W gap-close' with no mention of the animation.
audit.why: Empower is an auto-attack reset, so Jax's commit opens with an attack wind-up rather than a visible spell cast. The readable cue is the wind-up, not the button. For a champion with no dash this is the difference between reacting a beat early and reacting a beat late.
audit.corrected: The Empower wind-up is the cue to step back — by the time you see the leap it is already resolved.

audit.why: 36.36% over 11 games, carried consistently across both layers with a HARD 8/10 grade. No elo-tier language anywhere.

The spike timings already on disk are right: level 2-3 is Mel's only clean window, level 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms flips the duel, and the Trinity Force spike is Jax's takeover. Left alone apart from the Counter Strike numbers folded in.

notes: The packet's suspectNames entry for this matchup ('Solar Snare's' in wants.you[0], edit distance 2) is a false positive — Solar Snare is the correct name for Mel's E per champ-data/_kits/mel.json and the string is simply a possessive. No edit made on that basis. Note also that the '550-range' figures in this entry are correct as written: they refer to Mel's basic-attack range, not to Radiant Volley (which is 950). Several other Mel matchups misapply 550 to the Q; this one does not.
